cards.text: The prophet Amos is bringing the LORD's word to the house of Israel, a people who trample the poor (Amos 5:11). Some of them are longing for the Day of the LORD, counting down to it like it's PAYDAY. And Amos says, "Woe to you who long for the Day of the LORD!"

cards.question: Amos asks what the Day of the LORD will be for the people longing for it. What's his answer?

cards.text: Then Amos paints a picture. A man is running for his life from a lion.

cards.question: In Amos's picture, the man who gets away from the lion is safe from then on.

cards.text: He gets away from the lion, only to encounter a bear. That's like sneaking out of a meeting to dodge your boss and running STRAIGHT into your boss's boss.

cards.question: The man in Amos's picture finally makes it into his house and rests his hand against the wall. Then he's bitten by a ___.

cards.text: Amos says it again: the Day of the LORD will be darkness and not light, gloom with no brightness in it. Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, and trust me, nobody counts down the days to that.
Now the LORD Himself speaks. He's talking about Israel's worship: their feasts and their solemn assemblies.

cards.question: Israel keeps holding feasts and solemn assemblies. What does the LORD say about them?
The LORD says He will accept Israel's burnt offerings and grain offerings.

cards.text: Then the LORD says, "Take away from Me the noise of your songs!" Friend, He calls their songs NOISE.

cards.question: The LORD says He will listen to the music of Israel's harps.
Instead of Israel's feasts, offerings and songs, what does the LORD want to roll on like a river?
Along with justice, the LORD wants righteousness to flow like an ever-flowing stream.

cards.text: Then the LORD asks the house of Israel a question about their past. Did they bring Him sacrifices and offerings in the wilderness?

cards.question: The LORD asks about sacrifices and offerings during Israel's ___ years in the wilderness.

cards.text: Then He names what they've taken along with them: Sakkuth their king and Kaiwan their star god.

cards.question: What does the LORD call Sakkuth and Kaiwan?

cards.text: So the LORD, whose name is the God of Hosts, says what's coming. He will send them into exile.

cards.question: The LORD says He will send Israel into exile beyond ___.

findings.problem: Story card 11 has just told the baker "Take away from Me the noise of your songs!" and stressed that He calls their songs NOISE. That gives away the answer to card 12, which asks whether the LORD will listen to the music of their harps. Card 11 is a story card, not an answered choice, so the easy follow-up allowance doesn't apply.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later. Once a choice has been answered, the cards after it can build on that answer.

findings.problem: The question says "Instead of Israel's feasts, offerings and songs." That rules out both wrong answers: "Sacrifices" is an offering and "Praise" is a song. Only "Justice" is left.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: From card 8 on, the stop has no humor. Cards 15, 17 and 19 cover the wilderness question, the idols and the exile in plain narration. They read like a pleasant summary, not Papa Dorin. The only jokes are on cards 1, 5, 7 and 11.

rule.text: Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
